steps.text: Mix kale, red onion, and raisins in a large bowl.

Whisk yogurt, mayonnaise, sugar, lemon zest, and lemon juice together in a bowl; pour over the kale mixture and toss to coat. Refrigerate 2 hours to overnight. Sprinkle sunflower seeds over the salad and toss to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Kale Salad
raw_recipe.description: Make this creamy salad dressing for kale with lemon juice, lemon zest, and yogurt to tenderize freshly chopped kale for a vibrant flavor-packed salad.
raw_recipe.name: Creamy Kale Salad

recipeInstructions.text: Mix kale, red onion, and raisins in a large bowl.

Whisk yogurt, mayonnaise, sugar, lemon zest, and lemon juice together in a bowl; pour over the kale mixture and toss to coat. Refrigerate 2 hours to overnight. Sprinkle sunflower seeds over the salad and toss to serve.

review.reviewBody: Great recipe. I 'massaged' the torn kale in a bowl with a dash of kosher salt for 2-3 minutes to break down the fibres and make it more toothsome. I also added 1 Tbsp. of tahini to the dressing for an even creamier version and added dried cranberries. Thank you for an inspirational recipe!

This s is a great way to fix kale. I massaged my washed chopped kale with a tbsp. of olive oil, a tbsp. of fresh squeezed lemon juice, and a tsp. of kosher salt. I did not rinse after massaging. I substituted fresh orange zest and orange juice for the lemon in the dressing. I also substituted honey for the sugar. It is very good!

I have made this many times. My favorite Kale Salad. I only add a little Dijon mustard (gives it a little zip), I also lightly salt the kale and massage it.. Trick is to refrigerate it for at least 4-5 hours (do it in the morning). The longer it sits, the better it is. My husband loves it too.

Liked this! Tweaked. Added couple tablespoons Dijon to salad dressing; used SpinBlend/Miracle Whip instead of mayo. Added some sautéed onion and bacon bits. Subbed almonds for sunflower seeds. Used 6 oz yogurt instead of 4. Flavorful and relatively low fat.

Excellent salad. With kale being at the very top of the most nutrient-dense foods on this planet, we’re always looking for more ways, other than smoothies, to incorporate this superfood into our eating regime. Used an entire 6 ounce container of Greek yogurt (3/5 cup), and added 4 ounces of crumbled feta cheese and 1 tablespoon tahini. While the dressed out salad had a slight hint of bitterness which we found desirable, adding an extra step by massaging the kale will substantially remove the natural bitterness and tenderize it too (type ‘massage kale’ into your search engine to see different techniques). Nice recipe, QD&P.

This is a great recipe. I've made it as written and also with subs as once I didn't have Yogurt so used sour cream. I've also used cranraisins and pecans or I've diced apples and feta. Use your imagination. I always try to make enough for left overs. This recipe can also be made the day before. I recommend messaging the kale with a little olive oil, the lemon and a pinch of sea salt until it turns bright green and starts to soften, usually 3 to 5 minutes.

I quadrupled or maybe even quintuppled this recipe to bring a healthy treat to our vet for Vet Tech week, and probably caused some unequal ingredient usage, but it was delicious. Ok, I changed a lot - I added shredded red and green cabbage, used dried cranberries instead of raisins, used toasted salted slivered almonds in addition to the sunflower seeds, and used shallots instead of red onion, but it was still yum. (oh, after loading the photo, I remembered I added blueberries to it as well). I'm going to make it again right now, but for me to enjoy :)

Great recipe! So much you can do with that lemon-yogurt base! I sub'd honey for the sugar, craisins instead of raisins and added some fresh grated parmesan. I also added some chopped sweet red pepper. (Measurements are up to your liking). Something else to try would be spicy pecans or smoked almonds tossed on the top instead of the sunflower seeds(sweet/salty/spicy/mmmm). Or simply add some of your favorite spice to the dressing! Delish and healthy too!

I loved this! My husband liked it too but thought is was a little rich. Didn’t have yogurt so substituted with sour cream. Not sure how much that affected it. Added some Craisins & a little feta cheese to help offset the richness. We both agreed this should be on our rotation of salads.

I hate it when people change the recipe and give it bad reviews. OK. I've said it. I will step down from my soap box. I had everything BUT the yogurt so I chose to add more mayo instead of driving to the store. And WOW is this good!!! Will make it again, for sure!!
Delicious! I omitted the sugar, and used dried cranberries instead of raisins. Also added cucumbers.
really tasty - I did add chicken and bacon bits.
This recipe has become a favorite. I've shared it with friends and family, and all approved. Even if they think they don't like kale, they are surprised at the flavor and love it!

I didn't change anything other then adding pine nuts because that's what I had.
I did think it was too sweet so next time I'll add less sugar or more lemon juice.
This was quite a delightful, delicious and refreshing salad. I added raisins and some sliced almonds also along with the cranberries. I highly recommend this recipe.
So easy to make. Great flavours. I substituted scallions for red onions.
Hi grew a lot of kale in my garden this year and needs some interesting recipes. This one was a real hit. I used cranberries mistreat of raisins.

Wow, this salad is awesome! Especially the dressing! I made it exactly as written except to substitute dried cranberries for the raisins as we're not crazy about raisins. I can see substituting chopped grapes and maybe adding roasted almond slivers. I will definitely be making this recipe again and again!

This is really good, even though I didn't allow it to stand for the full two hours before serving. My husband, not a big kale fan, enjoyed it too. I made it exactly as written, including homemade raisins.
The dressing is very tasty and love this salad overall. The only change I made was chopping and lightly blanching the kale to make it less “chewy”/ more palatable.
